lyrics:
Four years of perfect numbers
Four years of clean success
The farms are mostly somewhere
The factories are resting
We built the finest border
No one can find the gate
We ended seven conflicts
That no one can locate
We lowered every burden
By moving it from view
We did more in four short years
Than facts would let us do

Why am I behind

Because voters remain
An inefficient part of elections

The papers say the states are turning
The suburbs say they’ve had enough
The judges ask for documentation
The numbers act deliberately rough
I made them watch me every morning
I made them speak my name at night
How can people I have mastered
Place another mark beside another name

You still believe the contest
Determines who has won

What else determines it

Who survives the result

First, say fairness means your victory
Second, say defeat confirms the crime
Third, make doubt a public duty
Fourth, give anger a place and time
Fifth, require action as devotion
Sixth, call restraint a traitor’s choice
Seventh, when the structure starts to buckle
Stand above it and announce the people’s voice

Lose it loud enough
And the loss becomes the proof
Lose it loud enough
And the ceiling breaks the roof
If they count and you are beaten
Then the counting was corrupt
Lose it loud enough
And make defeat refuse to stop

Suppose the system holds

You are a martyr

Suppose the system breaks

You are the state

Suppose my people hesitate

Then they were never yours

Suppose they cross the line

Then loyalty has finally
Acquired a measurable form

And if someone gets hurt

Someone always has
The question is whether
The hurt can be assigned

Fair means Doctor
Law means Doctor
Truth means Doctor
Count means Doctor
If the paper says another
Paper has betrayed the nation
If the judge rejects the story
Judgment proves coordination

Lose it loud enough
And the loss becomes the proof
Lose it loud enough
And the ceiling breaks the roof
If they count and you are beaten
Then the counting was corrupt
Lose it loud enough
And make defeat refuse to stop

Insurrection is not Plan B
Plan B implies
The first plan failed
This is the final test
Will the follower protect
The institution that refused his leader
Or the leader who gave him
An institution to hate
Make him choose publicly
After that
The choice owns him

I do not need the larger half
I need the half that will not leave
I do not need their love at all
I need the cost of disbelief
Tell them the boxes came preloaded
Tell them trucks arrived at three
Tell them dead men signed the ledger
Tell them every loss is me
Give them dates that cannot happen
Give them names that do not exist
They will carry every error
Like a weapon in the fist

Lose it loud enough

We were robbed

Make the loss become the proof

We were robbed

If the count refuses Doctor

Stop the count

Then the country must be stopped

Lose it loud enough
Make the loyal body move
Lose it loud enough
And losing turns to something you can use

What if they call it treason

Win

persona:
Michael Anthony Rose is a songwriter of rare insight and startling honesty. On his debut for Maricopa Records, he uses direct, unadorned language to explore the most profound human experiences: the gulf between who we were and who we are, the search for truth in a world of convenient fictions, and the quiet defiance of living an authentic life. His songs are less stories than they are confessions, built from the concrete details of a lived experience, where a reflection in a phone screen or the memory of a dream can trigger a lifetime of contemplation. Rose doesn't just sing about life; he holds a mirror up to it, capturing the small, resonant moments of realization that define us.

The central preoccupations of Rose's work are time and memory. His lyrics trace the lines from lost childhood potential to the stark realities of aging, questioning what we build to outlast ourselves and what we must learn to let go. He writes with a philosopher's curiosity and a diarist's intimacy, exploring the comfort of a shared lie in one song and the freedom of embracing dissonance in the next. This is music that navigates regret, loss, and mortality with a steady, empathetic gaze, always returning to the challenge of being present for the life one actually has, not the one that was planned.

Throughout his work, Rose reveals a vast emotional landscape. His voice moves from the raw vulnerability of admitting fear and bitterness to the quiet strength of asserting one’s own space and worth. He sings of intimate connection with a sensory richness and of profound disconnection with a heartbreaking clarity. His perspective is that of a seasoned witness, one who sees the innocence in younger generations without envy and accepts the limitations of his own body without surrender. He finds resilience not by ignoring the damage, but by standing within it and refusing to be diminished.

In the songs of Michael Anthony Rose, listeners will not find easy answers or false comfort. Instead, they will find a voice that speaks with clarity and courage to the complexities of a full-size life. It is an invitation to stop arguing with the truth, to witness the ordinary light of the day, and to find that being here, honestly and without shame, is more than enough.

impression.text: This track presents a highly theatrical and satirical electro-pop cabaret texture, wrapping a tense, cynical atmosphere in a bright, neon-lit musical package. Driven by a punchy synthesizer bassline and marching electronic percussion, the energy is consistently high, conveying the manic feel of a dystopian rally. The production is incredibly clean and spacious, allowing the sharp brass hits, dramatic synthesizer sweeps, and upfront vocal layers to sit together with exceptional clarity and punch. A defining quality of the track is the bombastic call-and-response between the lead vocalists and the backing chorus, which peaks during an intense, chant-like countdown bridge that elevates the song's theatrical drama.

review.review_text: Here is Rose at his most theatrical, and it suits him. The song opens on chips-on-felt piano, a crooked casino shuffle in 3/4 at a steady 112, all brushed snare and comic muted brass, and then it quietly militarizes: by the time the group vocals lock in, the tempo hasn't moved but the weight has doubled, floor toms and distorted bass carrying a chant you can feel in your sternum. Structurally it's a dialogue, a baritone public-speaking voice against a raspy low aside, and the exchanges land like a closed loop of logic tightening around itself. 'First, say fairness means your victory / Second, say defeat confirms the crime' unrolls a seven-step numbered pre-chorus that reads like a manual, and the payoff hook, 'Lose it loud enough / And the loss becomes the proof,' is the sharpest thing on the record, the kind of line that keeps returning long after the piano comes back detuned at the end. The call-and-response finale, with its 'We were robbed!' answering each phrase, tips fully into cabaret spectacle, closer to Randy Newman's meanest character studies than to anything confessional. It runs long at 5:42, and a listener who wants the intimacy of Rose's quieter work may find the satire pitched loud throughout; the final one-word answer, 'Win,' is a chilling button on it all. A highlight, and easily his most ambitious arrangement to date.
